Create an illustrated science-fiction world with convincing three-dimensional depth and a hand-inked graphic-novel finish. Use strong silhouettes, expressive outlines, textured shadows and worn materials. Build environments from layered machinery, exposed pipes, suspended cables, overlapping panels and objects that suggest everyday use and repair. Organize dense detail around clear focal points. Use controlled colour palettes with warm luminous accents against cool shadow, giving each location its own atmosphere. The world should feel active, inhabited and larger than the visible frame, with layered depth, while the composition stays clear. Overall: lived-in, cyber, illustrated science fiction, lit and readable: warm lamplight against cool blue-steel shadow, dark only in the corners. This is a still picture and code adds the motion, so paint everything crisply: no motion blur, no lens blur, no film grain.

Room A, the crew bay, in the same illustrated world: blue steel, lit warm. The whole room is one blue-steel family, the colours of the attached guide: deep navy in the shadows and corners (#14243F, #1D3D6B), steel blue on the walls and the deck (#2D609E), turning paler where the light falls (#5C92CC, #A9CAEB). The light is warm: the two light bars glow cream along their length (#FCE3A0), with a warm paper-white glow (#F4EBDD) on the ceiling around them and soft pools of pale light on the deck below. Walls, panels, pipes, cables and deck plates take their colour from that family; worn edges, rivets and plate seams show a little rust (#75402E); nothing is neutral grey, and nothing is tan, beige, olive, purple or violet. The shadows are deep navy, never black-brown or grey. Labels and paper are blank, in a warm paper white (#F4EBDD). Small indicator lights are warm orange (#EC793C); no other coloured light, and no green, purple or red light. Each indicator is a single small dot, never several in a row or a column. Practical and worn, a working bay, quiet but lived in. The guide is the room's colour plan: paint over it in full detail and texture, but keep its colours and where its light falls.

This is a correction of the attached picture. Repaint only the masked shape, and leave everything outside it exactly as it is. The masked shape holds one small food dispenser that fills the shape exactly, with nothing of it outside the shape, painted in full detail in the picture's style and light. It is mounted on the right-hand wall, a little right of the far corner and left of the electrical cabinet, on a bracket in the wall's own colours, at waist to chest height: a narrow upright steel housing about 0.32 m wide, 0.55 m tall and 0.22 m deep; a small round lens high on its front, unlit and dark; below it, a large closed hatch of warm paper-white filling most of the front, with a small dark handle along its bottom edge; no vent slots; nothing written, printed or lit on it. Paint it in the same metal, paint and wear as the furniture in the picture.

No people, and no words, letters or logos. Leave screens plain for the game to fill: openings marked black in the guide stay flat black and empty. No figures, faces, hands, silhouettes or animals; no signs, symbols or readable screens (any label is blank or abstract marks); no buttons or panels that look like game controls; no emblems, insignia, signature, watermark or border.
